summary: The article provides a largely accurate overview of the changes to unexplained income taxation under the hypothetical Income Tax Act, 2025, aligning well with expert opinions on proposed reforms, but some specific section mappings and penalty details require careful verification against official legislative text once available.

claims.claim: The Income Tax Act, 2025, introduces a distinction in taxation based on whether the disclosure is voluntary or detected by the tax authorities.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that the Income Tax Act, 2025 (or Finance Bill, 2026, which introduces it) differentiates between voluntary disclosure and departmental detection for unexplained income.

claims.claim: The Income Tax Act broadly categorises various forms of unexplained income under specific sections, primarily Sections 68, 69, 69A, 69B, 69C, and 69D of the Income Tax Act, 1961 (corresponding to Sections 102 to 106 of the Income Tax Act, 2025).
claims.note: Sources confirm that Sections 68-69D of the 1961 Act deal with unexplained income categories and that these correspond to Sections 102-106 of the Income Tax Act, 2025.

claims.claim: Under the previous regime, any income falling under Sections 68 to 69D was taxed at a flat rate of 60%. On top of this, a 25% surcharge and a 4% cess were levied, taking the effective tax rate to approximately 78%.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that under the previous regime (Income Tax Act, 1961, Section 115BBE), unexplained income was taxed at a flat 60%, with a 25% surcharge and 4% cess, leading to an effective rate of approximately 78%.

claims.claim: If this income was detected by the Assessing Officer and not offered voluntarily in the return, a penalty of 10% of the tax payable was imposed under Section 271AAC, pushing the overall burden to around 84%.
claims.note: Sources confirm that Section 271AAC of the Income Tax Act, 1961, imposed a 10% penalty on the tax payable under Section 115BBE if the unexplained income was detected and not voluntarily declared, leading to an overall burden of around 84%.

claims.claim: Under the Income Tax Act, 2025, if a taxpayer voluntarily discloses unexplained income in their return, the tax rate is significantly reduced to 30%. After including a 25% surcharge and 4% cess, the effective tax rate for voluntarily disclosed unexplained income comes down to approximately 39%.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that under the Income Tax Act, 2025, voluntary disclosure of unexplained income is taxed at a base rate of 30%, with a 25% surcharge and 4% cess, resulting in an effective rate of approximately 39%.

claims.claim: If, however, the unexplained income is detected by the Income Tax Department during an assessment or reassessment, it is specifically treated as "misreporting of income" under Section 439 of the Income Tax Act, 2025.
claims.note: Sources indicate that under the Income Tax Act, 2025, detected unexplained income is treated as misreporting of income under Section 439.

claims.claim: For misreporting, a penalty equal to 200% of the tax payable on such income is levied under Section 439. This means that for ₹100 of unexplained income detected by the tax department, the total burden rises to approximately 99% (including tax, surcharge, cess, and 200% penalty).
claims.note: Sources confirm that Section 439 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, levies a 200% penalty on the tax payable for misreporting of income, and calculations show this leads to an approximate 99% total burden on the unexplained income.

claims.claim: If the taxpayer accepts the addition, does not file an appeal, and makes timely payment of tax, interest, and penalty, the penalty can be reduced to 120%, bringing the effective rate to 75%.
claims.note: Sources confirm that the penalty for detected unexplained income can be reduced to 120% if the taxpayer accepts the addition and makes timely payments, leading to an effective rate of 75%.
